materiality: DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 MegaAttention dummy-prefill or autotuning can produce NaN candidate scores; the predecessor treated NaN as invalid padding after top-k, underfilled the active sparse-block prefix, and could repeat one block hundreds of times where DeepGEMM expects unique indices.

The repair preserves top-k selected NaN-scored block IDs while still reserving -inf as padding; it prevents the observed invalid sparse prefix but explicitly does not sanitize or explain the upstream source of NaNs.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM source/image, DeepSeek-V4.1 model/config, DSpark/DeepGEMM versions, TP topology, graph mode and accelerator identity.

Reproduce the known-bad predecessor with zero, NaN and mixed-NaN candidate scores; assert the invalid active-prefix or repeated-index condition, then require the candidate to retain selected block IDs and preserve uniqueness and padding invariants.

Run finite-score controls against the predecessor or reference selector, captured failing-row replay, short and long prompt traffic, autotuning and target/draft graph capture; candidate must not change finite selection semantics.

Investigate and separately receipt the upstream NaN source; success of this storage repair must not be claimed as numerical sanitization. Preserve incumbent rollback and mark unavailable hardware/topology UNAVAILABLE.

materiality: GLM-5.3-Flash KpoolTail is a fixed circular buffer, but the generic slot-mapping kernel indexes by unbounded position divided by block size; sufficiently long prompts can read a neighboring request row or outside the block-table allocation and trigger a memory access fault.
The upstream repair makes KpoolTail opt out of the generic mapper and retains its tailored circular slot mapping; this is a memory-safety and request-isolation boundary, not a performance tweak.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM source/image, GLM-5.3-Flash artifact, ROCm/AITER sparse-MLA configuration, KV layout, max sequence length, concurrency and accelerator/runtime identity.

Run the known-bad predecessor poison-row and out-of-bounds regression plus long-context reproduction, including the affected 500k-input regime when hardware capacity permits; prove the candidate never derives a KpoolTail slot from neighboring-request or past-table memory.

Verify tailored circular mapping under request interleaving, slot reuse, cancellation, long-context boundary positions and concurrency; compare generated output plus representative accuracy to the incumbent path.
Keep generic slot mapping enabled for unaffected KV groups, retain rollback, and classify missing long-context hardware as UNAVAILABLE rather than inferring safety from unit tests.

materiality: On ROCm, native CPU KV offload could allocate the shared mmap path and have every worker register the full region, causing cudaHostRegister failures and startup stalls at large offload sizes.

The repair routes ROCm to private per-rank pinned tensors and disables replicated-layout assumptions that would otherwise acknowledge rank-local stores without a shared medium; CUDA shared-region behavior is intentionally unchanged.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM source/image, ROCm driver/runtime, accelerator model/count, TP topology, KV dtype, offload size/backend and model identity.

Reproduce the predecessor shared-registration failure or equivalent bounded negative control on affected ROCm, then prove private per-rank pinned allocation reaches readiness without silent replicated-layout admission.

Exercise cold prompt, GPU eviction, CPU-to-GPU reload and post-eviction replay across multiple ranks; require output parity and transfer/accounting receipts with no cross-rank data loss or stale-block reuse.
Run a CUDA control proving its shared-region behavior is unchanged, measure host-pinned memory cost of the ROCm private layout, preserve rollback, and mark absent ROCm capacity UNAVAILABLE.

materiality: SGLang changed the FlashInfer CUTLASS and CuTe DSL MoE fused-finalize default from enabled to disabled for numerical-accuracy reasons while retaining an explicit performance opt-in.

Upstream performance sweeps show nontrivial workload-dependent cost, but the PR explicitly did not run model accuracy tests and did not measure numerical-error reduction; SZL must not promote either default from the upstream rationale alone.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact SGLang source/image, FlashInfer packages, CUDA/SM target, model/quantization mode, MoE runner, EP/TP topology and fused-finalize environment value.

Evaluate old-default enabled versus new-default disabled plus deterministic-mode controls on identical prompts/tensors; measure logits/output error against an independent trusted reference and repeated-run variance across CUTLASS and supported CuTe DSL paths.

Measure latency and throughput separately from accuracy across representative token counts and W4A4/W4A16 modes; an accuracy gain must be evidenced, and a performance tradeoff must never be relabeled as correctness.
Keep the upstream performance opt-in explicit, do not silently re-enable fused finalize, preserve rollback to the currently qualified behavior, and leave untested hardware/backends UNQUALIFIED.

materiality: Balanced device-map sizing considered the largest no-split block but not a larger childless leaf such as embeddings or lm_head; large unquantized leaves can make every capped device look too small, collapse placement onto the last device, spill to CPU and make 4-bit loading fail despite ample aggregate GPU budget.

The upstream repair sizes the buffer from the largest leaf as well as the largest no-split block and adds accelerator-free regression coverage; deployment qualification still needs an actual representative quantized load.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact Transformers/Accelerate/quantization package versions, model config/checkpoint, dtype/quantization, requested max_memory map and target accelerator topology.
Run the known-bad meta/fake-budget case with a large-vocabulary leaf and candidate regression, then verify an actual representative 4-bit model load where aggregate bounded GPU memory is sufficient.

Assert placement never silently spills required quantized modules to CPU/disk when the declared budget can accommodate the model, while preserving valid CPU/disk offload behavior when explicitly requested or genuinely necessary.
Compare placement map, peak memory, load success and representative inference output against the qualified baseline; preserve rollback and treat unavailable representative hardware as UNAVAILABLE.

materiality: DeepSeek-V4 DSML tool calls can omit the optional string attribute on a parameter; the predecessor parser could drop or mis-handle that parameter, corrupting structured tool arguments.
The repair covers Python and Rust frontend parsing and related V3.2/V4.1 schema paths; agent tool execution must be qualified on the exact parser/frontend actually serving requests.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM source/image, selected Python or Rust frontend, DeepSeek-V4 model/template/tokenizer and tool schema.

Use a known-bad omitted-string fixture and require the candidate to retain and coerce the parameter correctly in complete and streaming parses across chunk boundaries; execute the same semantic case through both frontends where supported.

Add controls for explicit string=true/false, booleans, numbers, nested JSON, whitespace, multiple parameters/tools, malformed tags and adversarial closing-tag text; require no argument loss, type drift or cross-tool contamination.

Bind parsed tool-call receipts to the raw model-output hash before any downstream tool execution, preserve fallback/rollback, and keep external effectors disabled until the serving parser is qualified.
